posts.text: A good read & worth considering. Although I think it buries the lead a bit. It is probably true that the time of Americans as joiners that lasted from the 1890s-1960s was unusual but the question then,for me,is what made it possible&how the balance between community&autonomy could be struck again.

posts.text: My theory on this is American capitalism is now so bad it forces people to move away for education, jobs, and better opportunities; disincentivizes doing hobbies for fun; and takes time and energy away from leisure sports, volunteering, mentoring, union organizing, and other community activities.

posts.text: I don't have a theory as to the cause (though this thread seems very astute to me), but from talking about my community involvement, I think a lot of people really flip out at the (small) amount of distress tolerance and conflict management necessary for interacting closely with other people.

posts.text:
As someone who covers the religious left a lot, I find this piece wild.

But it’s also a reminder of why the religious left is often the epicenter of *activism* and particularly *protest* on the left: they’re the ones with the most pre-organized communities, as it were.

Also…
